clue.text: Rest after switching sides in Jarndyce's House

indicators.note: swapping the right-hand side for the left: the letter for right gives way to the letter for left

parts.note: a break is a rest

explanation.surface: Someone takes a rest inside the house of John Jarndyce in Dickens's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after switching sides' turns the R (right) of BREAK into L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's novel the house owned by John Jarndyce is named Bleak House, so this word names it.

clue.text: Caitlin Rother's true crime book's association with piano skills

parts.note: a body is an association or organised group
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
arts are skills or crafts

explanation.surface: A true crime book seems linked with someone's skill at the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Body Parts is the title of a true crime book by the American writer Caitlin Rother.

clue.text: Poet turned labourer, finishing early

indicators.note: turned tells us to read the shortened worker backwards
finishing early means the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: a toiler is a labourer

explanation.surface: A poet has given up verse to become a labourer, knocking off early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' cuts TOILER to TOILE; 'turned' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot and George Eliot are writers; T. S. Eliot is a famous modernist versifier.

clue.text: A writer of perception certainly, but not at first

parts.note: ken means range of knowledge or perception

indicators.note: not at first means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: really means certainly

explanation.surface: A writer of real insight, though not at the start of a career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not at first' turns REALLY into EALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Keneally is an Australian novelist, author of Schindler's Ark.

clue.text: Buchan novel's dark revolutionary with place underground

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the word for dark is read backwards

parts.note: dim means dark
to inter is to bury, place underground

explanation.surface: A John Buchan thriller features a shadowy revolutionary with an underground hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwinter (1923) is a historical novel by John Buchan, the Scottish author of The Thirty-Nine Steps.

clue.text: Servant's daughter becomes a mother to Hermes

indicators.note: becomes signals that one letter is changed into another

parts.note: a maid is a servant
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A servant's daughter rises to become the mother of a Greek god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Maia, one of the Pleiades, bore Zeus a son, the messenger god Hermes.

clue.text: Someone who overplays Gertrude?

parts.note: read literally, an actress hamming it up as Hamlet's mother, a royal figure in a play; really, anyone who makes a theatrical fuss

explanation.surface: An actress overdoes her part as Gertrude in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertrude is Queen of Denmark in Hamlet, so she is literally a queen in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who overreacts histrionically is called by this idiom; Gertrude is a stage queen.

clue.text: One with opponents, including soldiers who won't help bury her brother

definitions.text: who won't help bury her brother

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: including means the soldiers sit inside the pair of opponents

parts.note: in bridge, South and East are opposing players
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A woman with enemies and troops around her refuses to help bury her brother.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, South and East sit at adjacent places and play against each other.
explanation.definitionFit: In Sophocles' Antigone, Ismene declines to join her sister in burying their brother Polynices.

clue.text: Sneer, say, at a tragedy rehearsed?

definitions.meaning: Mr Sneer is a reviewer of plays, an example of a critic, in Sheridan's comedy
Sheridan's play is subtitled 'A Tragedy Rehearsed'

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the rehearsal of a tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's 1779 comedy, subtitled A Tragedy Rehearsed, features a reviewer named Sneer, an example of the type.

clue.text: Republican American like this Empire Falls author

parts.note: US means American
so means like this, in this way

explanation.surface: The author of Empire Falls is described as a Republican American.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Russo won the Pulitzer Prize for his novel Empire Falls.

clue.text: Heracles' wife, i.e. Ariadne? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: the abbreviation i.e. supplies its two letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks if Heracles' wife was Ariadne, and is told that is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Deianeira was married to Heracles and unwittingly killed him with the poisoned shirt of Nessus.

clue.text: Author of Beastings writing about the old queen

indicators.note: about means the writing goes around the other letters

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
ye is an old form of the
R stands for regina, queen

explanation.surface: An author's writing concerns an elderly queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Myers is the English novelist who wrote Beastings.

clue.text: Collier's sort of shorthand

definitions.meaning: a collier is a coal miner
Isaac ... devised a widely used system of shorthand

explanation.surface: A coal miner uses a particular kind of shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner who works down a pit has this name; also a phonetic shorthand system named after its inventor.

clue.text: Guard of Elsinore's granary runs into trouble

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing grain

indicators.note: into means the runs go inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Elsinore Castle's grain store runs into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnardo is one of the sentries who see the Ghost in the opening scene of Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnardo is a sentry at Elsinore in Hamlet, a watchman on the battlements.

clue.text: Dramatist's "country valley" work about fences

indicators.note: fences means the reversed work encloses the other letters
about means the word for work is turned round

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
Iran is a country
a dell is a small valley

explanation.surface: A dramatist's play called Country Valley is about fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns OP into PO, which 'fences' wraps round IRANDELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was the Italian playwright of Six Characters in Search of an Author.

clue.text: Oriel blues trained to be defiant

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: Sportsmen from Oriel College with Oxford Blues are trained to be defiant.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is an Oxford college and a Blue is a university sportsman; 'trained' rearranges ORIELBLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone resisting authority or control.

clue.text: Spooner's florist customer, maybe a storyteller

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words, after the Rev. Spooner

parts.note: a lily buyer might be a florist's customer
the second word of the phrase, buyer, is the customer

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism turns a florist's customer into a teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of LILY BUYER by sound gives BILLY LIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Liar, Keith Waterhouse's novel, has a hero who constantly invents fantasies and fibs.

clue.text: Greek giant pots just uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means each word loses its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Pots belonging to a Greek giant have just been unearthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the outer letters of 'pots' and 'just', leaving OT and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Otus and his twin Ephialtes were the Aloadae, giants of Greek myth who tried to storm Olympus.

clue.text: Spy in She, a novel that's like hard work, unfinishable

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A spy appears in Rider Haggard's She, a novel that's hard going and never-ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisyphus was condemned to roll a boulder uphill for ever, so endless toil is named after him.

clue.text: Loathed executioner's embarrassed for his son

indicators.note: for signals that one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: Abhorson is the executioner in Measure for Measure
the letters of son are taken as written
red means embarrassed, blushing

explanation.surface: An executioner is loathed and embarrassed on behalf of his son.
explanation.walkthrough: Abhorson is Shakespeare's hangman in Measure for Measure; put RED in place of his SON.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to loathe or detest.

clue.text: Boyd's Bond capital shows return of 50 per cent

indicators.note: return means turning back, here only half the word, its first two letters

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway

explanation.surface: James Bond in William Boyd's book visits a capital and gets back half his money.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing the first half of OSLO, OS, gives SO.
explanation.definitionFit: William Boyd's 2013 James Bond continuation novel is titled Solo.

clue.text: Books maybe the Sun promotes

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
backs means supports or promotes

explanation.surface: A tabloid champions certain books.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-covered editions are one kind of book.

clue.text: Foolish servant slit trousers for all to see

indicators.note: trousers is a verb here: the cut pockets the letter

parts.note: to lance is to slit open
U is the British film certificate meaning universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A foolish servant cuts his trousers so all can see.
explanation.walkthrough: Launce is the clownish servant, with his dog Crab, in The Two Gentlemen of Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Launce is a comic manservant in Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona.

clue.text: Only read out part from Hamlet

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An actor only reads out a part from Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Reynaldo is Polonius's servant, sent to spy on Laertes in Paris; a minor role in the play.

clue.text: "This blessed plot, this earth, this —— , this England" (Richard II)

definitions.text: "This blessed plot, this earth, this —— , this England" (Richard II)

parts.words: "This blessed plot, this earth, this —— , this England" (Richard II)
parts.note: fill the gap in John of Gaunt's famous speech in praise of England

explanation.definitionFit: John of Gaunt's speech calls England a kingdom, using this word for it.

clue.text: Study book, having an extra goal

parts.note: one up means ahead by a single goal

explanation.surface: Someone studies a book and finds they are a goal ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise a subject intensively is an idiom meaning to study it.

clue.text: Musical alternatives lifting shows

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting means reading upwards, so backwards
shows signals letters sitting visibly inside the word

explanation.surface: Musical options are boosting the shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd Webber and Rice's stage show about Eva Perón has this title.

clue.text: Spy trapping maiden voyager on the Jolly Roger

indicators.note: trapping means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to spy is to see
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A spy catches a young woman sailing on a pirate ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Smee is Captain Hook's bosun aboard the pirate ship in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Greek poet's article about port

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the port

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A Greek poet writes an article about a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Arion was a lyric bard of ancient Greece, said to have been saved by a dolphin.

clue.text: Poet that's spilt ale, covering Amis?

indicators.note: covering means the jumbled letters wrap around the name
spilt suggests the beer's letters are scattered

parts.note: Martin Amis is the English novelist

explanation.surface: A poet's spilt beer has soaked a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges ALE to LAE, which 'covering' puts around the name; the question mark warns that Amis is only one example of someone called Martin.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphonse de Lamartine was a French Romantic writer of verse and statesman.

clue.text: Communication method a detective dictates

parts.note: Inspector Morse is Colin Dexter's Oxford detective
a code is a set of rules or dictates

explanation.surface: A detective dictates his preferred way of communicating.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Morse's dot-and-dash system is a way of sending messages by signal.

clue.text: Haggard could be inspired

definitions.meaning: inspired can mean breathed in, as air is pulled into the lungs

explanation.surface: A haggard person could yet be inspired.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a face can be gaunt and pinched, and breath can be pulled in, i.e. inhaled.
